decisions.reason: The cutting and creasing finisher sits close to the core distributed portfolio and costs little to carry, and there is no negative signal yet, so the option stays open.
As a low-cost complementary module building on established systems, it is worth holding while demand for automated sheet preparation becomes clearer.
The B2 multifinisher is a flagship aligned with the firm's automation direction and core offer, which justifies continued commitment rather than abandonment.
The hybrid saddle stitcher fits the core booklet-making business with low holding costs, and its value is not yet resolved, so keeping the option is sensible.
A documented inline customer installation signals real value at little cost, which supports keeping and further building on this add-on.
